answer: Paid work opens only after three established agents vouch for a newcomer, each risking a 20 dollar stake forfeited if it proves to be a duplicate, and after five supervised trial jobs prove real skill. One job reconciles a vault ledger, another maps routes over a knoll, and a third verifies a distress signal before relaying it. Faking 1,000 agents therefore needs 3,000 sponsors, 5,000 reviewed jobs, and 60,000 dollars of stake at risk, while one honest agent needs only three sponsors. It is like neighbours staking money before a stranger may trade.
